newsitem.title: USA: Incinerator subsidy bill fails in Illinois House.
newsitem.headline: Incinerator subsidy bill fails in Illinois House.

text.p: Legislation to restore a state subsidy to two bond-financed waste-to-energy incinerators failed on third reading in the Illinois House on Thursday.
The bill to assist incinerators in two suburbs south of Chicago had faced opposition from House Speaker Michael Madigan and the Chicago-based Environmental Law & Policy Center.

The facilities in Robbins and Ford Heights would cost Illinois more than $700 million over a 20-year period and the defeat of the legislation "is wonderful news," policy center staff attorney Alexander Ewing said in a prepared statement.
A spokesman for Foster Wheeler Corp, the Clinton, N.J.-based developer of the Robbins incinerator, was not available for comment on Friday.
The subsidy's repeal has imperiled more than $500 million of tax-exempt, unrated bonds that were sold for three projects, including $320 million of debt for the Robbins project.
Only the two facilities were financed, built and received the necessary governmental orders and permits to be eligible for the subsidy.
Developers have also filed state court challenges to the repeal of the subsidy that Gov. Jim Edgar signed more than a year ago.
The subsidy would have guaranteed the incinerators a higher rate at which they could sell the electricity they produced to public utilities.
The legislation had been sponsored by Rep. Harold Murphy, D-Markham.

"Under this bill, Illinois would have spent twice as much tax money every year on two incinerators as it spends on school lunches," Ewing said. "This bill would also have subsidized pollution that threatens our kids' health."
